audios.title: Discussing a tree-planting project
audios.transcript:
Mia: So, for our project, we’re evaluating the tree-planting scheme on the hills outside town. Where do you want to start, Leo?
Leo: I thought the main question was simple: did they plant enough trees? The council’s target was fifty thousand, and they planted more than that.
Mia: True, but our tutor said the number planted isn’t the best measure. What matters is how many survived.
Leo: Good point. According to the report, about forty per cent died in the first two years.
Mia: That’s quite high. The report blames the dry summer, but I think the bigger problem was the type of tree. They planted a fast-growing species that isn’t native to this area.
Leo: Why did they choose it?
Mia: It was cheaper and grew quickly, so the hills would look green sooner. But native trees support more insects and birds.
Leo: So in our evaluation, we should compare the survival of native and non-native trees.
Mia: Exactly. And we should mention that local people weren’t involved. Volunteers from the city did the planting, and nobody came back to water the young trees.
Leo: What would we recommend, then?
Mia: Smaller areas planted with native species, and a local group responsible for looking after them for the first three years.
Leo: I agree. Shall we present our findings as a poster or a short talk?
Mia: A poster, I think – we can show the photos from our site visit.
Leo: Fine. I’ll design the poster, and you write the recommendations.
